newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls foresees growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls foresees growth in 1997.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc, the giant in controls and automotive systems, expects both groups to grow "at good rates" in 1997, a company statement said Thursday.
The statement said the company foresaw its automotive systems group raising its sales by 25 percent to 30 percent through market share gains and recent acquisitions.
It also saw its controls group boosting its revenues by 10 percent to 15 percent as the non-residential buildings market grows throughout the world, it said.
Johnson Controls reported a fully-diluted share of $1.19 in fiscal first-quarter earnings against $0.98 for the same period the previous year.
The company's first quarter ended December 31.
The statement said the automotive systems group enjoyed an increase in sales during the quarter to $2.0 billion against $1.4 billion for the same period last year.

"(About) two-thirds of the group's revenue increase reflects the October 1996 acquisition of Prince, an interior systems company based in Michigan, and Roth Freres, a French seating and interior systems company, acquired in December 1995," it said.
The statement said sales for the controls group increased 16 percent to $731.2 million for the first quarter, up from $632.5 million in 1995.
"The increase was led by higher integrated facility management activity in Europe and North America compared with the prior year," it said.
